What are your thoughts on the game thus far? From the gameplay I've watched, Splatoon looks like a lot of fun, but I'm having a hard time justifying the price tag. Is there a lot of content? How do you feel about the replay value?
Thoughts about the game - worth the money?

I'll start by saying that I'm not one to ever buy games new or full price, I'm poor like that. However, after playing the testfire, I scrounged up whatever cash I could find and bought the game first day. Loved it.
It's a fresh new shooter and it feels fantastic. The focus is on the online battles though, so if that's not your thing then the game won't really be worth it since that's where most of the replayability is at. There is a single player mode that is quite enjoyable and is great to get you use to the controls, especially if you want to use the motion controls which I find work quite well, but I've never actually been a fan of shooters on consoles so I can't say anything about using the stick option. In any case, the single player mode unlocks some weapon variants that may be to your liking but they're not a big deal. And if you want to throw more money at Nintendo, you could always buy a Splatoon Amiibo to extend the single player and get some spiffy cloths.
So really, if you're into competitive shooters, I'd recommend it. It's fun, the soundtrack is amazing, and the fans are pretty amusing. Even if you don't have a lot of time to play, it's fine since the matches go quickly and lobbies fill up fast. Not a whole lot of waiting between gameplay, which is nice.

Just some thoughts: I'm not a fan of multiplayer games at all, particularly arena shooters, but this game just grabbed me. There's really a fair amount of tactical depth once you start figuring out how the game works. Trying to decide how to value spending your time painting this area or that, whether to engage an enemy or flee, etc. The single-player is a surprisingly fun platforming experience, though not super long. Maybe took somewhere between 5-8 hours to get through it. As for content, there really aren't a lot of maps, but that doesn't matter a whole lot. It's more about learning the ins and outs of the ones that are there, and they are releasing new ones every once in a while anyhow. Also, there are a fair number of outfit pieces to put on your squid/kid, and to collect them all would take quite a while. And of course, there's something intensely satisfying about painting the arena in your team's color.

I have clocked in around 60 hours, and I'm not getting tired of the game at all.
